Below is everything you’ll need to send your “malicious” vote for **22.242.75.136** to VirusTotal V5. I’ve given both a quick‑look `curl` one‑liner and a short Python script so you can pick whichever fits best into your workflow. --- ### Quick reference – what’s happening? | Step | What happens | |------|--------------| | **Endpoint** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/risk` | | **Method** | `POST` | | **Auth header** | `Authorization: Bearer ` (` = key_four`) | | **Payload** | `{ "type": "vote", "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious" }}` | VirusTotal will record this *suggested* verdict. It won’t instantly change the public reputation score—other analysts’ votes and automated scans still influence it—but it does add your input to their internal database. --- ## 1️⃣ One‑line `curl` ```bash curl -X POST \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-apikey: key_four" \ # <-- replace with your real key --data '{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}' \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/risk ``` ⚠️ If you’re running this from a shell where spaces could break things, wrap the URL in single quotes instead of double ones. --- ## 2️⃣ Minimal Python example (requests) ```python import json import requests api_key = "key_four" target_ip = "22.242.75.136" url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{target_ip}/risk" payload = { "type": "vote", "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious" } } headers = { "accept": "application/json", "content-type": "application/json", "x-apikey": api_key, } response = requests.post(url, data=json.dumps(payload), headers=headers) print("Status:", response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` If you don’t have `requests`, install it first: ```bash pip install requests ``` --- ## 📌 Things to keep in mind | Topic | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Rate limiting** | V5 allows ~60 calls/minute per account. Your single vote stays well below that. | | **Vote persistence** | Votes stay attached to the object until removed or overwritten by another analyst. | | **Confidence & tags** | Optional extras: `"confidence"` (0–100) and `"tags"` array. Example:
`{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious","confidence":80,"tags":["phishing"]}}`. | | **Error handling** | A non‑200 status means something went wrong. Common errors include invalid API key (`401 Unauthorized`) or malformed JSON (`400 Bad Request`). | | **Documentation** | Full details at [VT Docs → Voting](https://developers.virustotal.com/reference/post-ip-addresses-id-risk). | Feel free to tweak the payload or integrate this call into whatever automation pipeline you already run!
